channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: 10 African countries with the weakest currencies in February 2026
item.description: A weak currency has real, sometimes unpleasant repercussions for people, businesses, and governments alike, as countries throughout Africa that have been subjected to prolonged devaluation are discovering.

item.title: Canadian mining giant discovers rare earth and critical mineral in Botswana amid U.S.–China supply race
item.description: Canadian mineral exploration company Tsodilo Resources Limited has confirmed a significant rare earth and critical minerals discovery in Botswana, positioning Canada within an intensifying global competition led by the United States and China to secure strategic supply chains.

item.title: African entrepreneur of the Month: Meet the defence-tech founders Western billionaires are betting their dollars on
item.description: Very few African startups can claim backing from figures such as Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, Lux Capital’s Josh Wolfe, investor Antonio Gracias and actor-entrepreneur Jared Leto; let alone have some publicly express their support. Terra Industries now finds itself in precisely that position.

item.title: Nigeria expands oil arsenal with new crude grade, exports set to hit global markets next month
item.description: Nigeria’s state oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC), will begin exporting a new light, sweet crude grade known as Cawthorne from March.

item.title: Angola seeks $4.8b Chinese loan for Lobito refinery build
item.description: Angola’s state oil company, Sonangol, is seeking a $4.8 billion loan from Chinese financial institutions to accelerate construction of the new refinery in the Atlantic port of Lobito, a move that could mark its first major borrowing from China in seven years.

item.title: Ghana moves to turn gold smuggling crisis into a $20 billion opportunity
item.description: Ghana is embarking on an ambitious gold-sector makeover, announcing plans to divert approximately 127 metric tons of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold into official trade each year in an effort to enhance foreign-exchange profits and reduce years of smuggling losses.

item.title: The 10 African countries where food prices will rise the most in 2026
item.description: A new global food inflation outlook released by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) projects sharp divergences in food price movements across 160 countries in 2026, with several African economies expected to record some of the steepest increases worldwide.

item.title: Nigeria targets $30 billion tax revenue in 2026 as lawmakers seek clarity
item.description: Nigeria is aiming to generate about $30.1 billion in tax and royalty revenue in 2026, signalling an increasingly ambitious fiscal push by the administration as it leans on reforms to strengthen public finances.

item.title: Ghana cocoa buyers owe banks up to $750m amid sector crisis
item.description: Ghana’s cocoa sector is facing mounting financial pressure, with licensed buyers owing banks between $650 million and $750 million in debts, according to the association representing them. This situation is squeezing liquidity in the supply chain just as the country’s banks continue their recovery from a severe economic downturn.

item.title: US marks strategic return to the Sahel with $147M health deal in Burkina Faso
item.description: The United States is signaling a renewed strategic push into West Africa’s volatile Sahel region, sealing a $147 million health deal with Burkina Faso in a move that blends humanitarian support with geopolitical recalibration.
